summary: Druckenmiller describes his macro style: forecast the economy from leading-industry stocks, size concentrated bets, and wait for fat pitches. In 2022 he saw a hard landing as probable because inflation above 5% has never been tamed without a recession, and was cautious on bonds and short on energy supply.

coverage.note: soft vs hard landing, inflation above 5% rules, excess savings
stocks as lead indicator, bond signal tainted
trucking, homebuilder signals; price action vs news
bear market toolkit, positioning, bonds problem
dollar, energy, crypto vs Nasdaq, bitcoin vs gold
bitcoin vs gold, work ethic, retail bull-market geniuses
2000 sabbatical, Ed Hyman regression, Treasuries trade
lessons of break, planned trigger, inflation/union
advice, change vs present, Covid over-earners
growth bias, cyclicals, big tech, energy trade

claims.speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller
claims.quote: they were still buying bonds in March of 22, and they were still not even pivoting verbally until November
claims.claim: The Fed's slow recognition of inflation (QE until March 2022, no verbal pivot until November) was costly because assets bought in that period will lose money.
claims.indicator: Fed balance sheet and forward guidance
claims.direction: risk assets down after late Fed pivot

claims.speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller
claims.quote: A lot of very good companies um have been de-rated 60, 70% without a whole lot of change in fundamentals.
claims.claim: The bubble burst shows up more in de-rated individual stocks (60-70%) than in the S&P index, so valuations improved relative to fundamentals.

claims.speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller
claims.quote: But we've never had a soft landing after inflation's gotten above 4 and 1/2%.
claims.claim: Soft landings are rare (two or three in history) and none occurred once inflation exceeded 4.5%, so a soft landing is a long shot.
claims.testable: yes - historical inflation episodes vs recessions

claims.speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller
claims.quote: once inflation gets above 5%, it's never come down unless uh Fed funds have gotten above the CPI.
claims.claim: Historically inflation above 5% has never fallen unless Fed funds exceeded CPI; with CPI at 8% that is unlikely given the asset bubble.
claims.direction: inflation stays high unless real rate positive

claims.speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller
claims.quote: once once inflation's got above 5%, to use your word, it's never been tamed without a recession.
claims.claim: Inflation above 5% has never been tamed without a recession, so he assumes a recession in 2023.

claims.speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller
claims.quote: there should have been many many many bankruptcies, which have been buried by QE.
claims.claim: Disruption would normally cause many bankruptcies, but QE suppressed them, so a rate rise to 8% would cause material destruction.

claims.speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller
claims.quote: a trillion and a half to two trillion of excess savings now. So it may take some time to work through that savings.
claims.claim: Excess household savings of $1.5-2tn delay the recession as they are spent down.

claims.speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller
claims.quote: stocks tend to lead the fundamentals by somewhere between 6 and 12 months.
claims.claim: Stocks lead the economy by 6-12 months, so industry stock moves act as a forecasting signal.

claims.speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller
claims.quote: if the leading industries are turning up or turning down, that's a signal. And that's worked beautifully historically.
claims.claim: He forecasts the economy from leading industries (housing, capital goods, retail) versus lagging ones using bottom-up stock analysis instead of traditional macro data.
claims.indicator: leading vs lagging industry stock performance

claims.speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller
claims.quote: the bond market has not signaled anything because the central banks took it upon themselves to manipulate bond prices
claims.claim: Under QE the 10-year yield lost its signal value, so bond market views on growth should be discounted.

claims.speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller
claims.quote: they've all declined 50% from the high. Another industry that's been incredibly pressured and has been trucking. Um and they're down 40% from the high
claims.claim: Homebuilders (-50%) and trucking (-40%) falling despite record earnings signals economic trouble 6-12 months ahead.

claims.speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller
claims.quote: retail appears to be much weaker than it should be given what the so-called GDP numbers are printing
claims.claim: Weak retail stocks versus GDP prints are an early warning, but retail is distorted by Covid shifts so read with care.

claims.speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller
claims.quote: A lot of these things have longer lead times, like 6 months to a year.
claims.claim: Do not call recession immediately from these stock signals because lead times are 6 to 12 months.

claims.speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller
claims.quote: We used to call it price action versus news. And it used to be an incredible indicator of security prices.
claims.claim: Price action versus news (stock up on bad news, down on good) was a strong indicator but is weakened by efficiency, hedge funds and central bank manipulation.

claims.speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller
claims.quote: I've always made even higher returns in bear markets than bull markets. But the way I did it was just pretty much ignore equities, take them off the table, buy bonds, buy treasuries and go home.
claims.claim: His traditional bear-market playbook is long Treasuries, which may fail with 8% inflation and 3% yields.
claims.conditions: fails with high inflation and low yields

claims.speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller
claims.quote: a matrix of short fixed income short stocks and not doing a whole lot in currencies and owning some of the key commodities
claims.claim: Positioning in the past 6-8 months: short fixed income, short stocks, long oil, copper and gold.
claims.direction: short bonds and stocks, long commodities

claims.speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller
claims.quote: if you get aggressive in a bear market on the short side you can get your head ripped off in rallies.
claims.claim: In a bear market, aggressive shorts get hurt in sharp rallies, so he waits for a fat pitch.

claims.speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller
claims.quote: I will be surprised if sometime in the next 6 months I'm not short the dollar. 14 trillion dollars has come in here because we were the first to tighten.
claims.claim: He expects to be short the dollar within 6 months as $14tn of inflows driven by the Fed tightening first reverse.

claims.speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller
claims.quote: because of the transition to ESG, we look to be short energy for 5 or 10 years
claims.claim: He expects energy supply to be short for 5-10 years because ESG limits investment, supporting energy longs.

claims.speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller
claims.quote: there certainly seems to be a strong correlation between crypto and the Nasdaq.
claims.claim: Crypto correlates strongly with Nasdaq, so he uses it as a risk indicator.

claims.speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller
claims.quote: Bitcoin is highly cyclical, gold is counter-cyclical historically.
claims.claim: Bitcoin acts as risk-on inflation asset and gold as the bear-phase asset: own Bitcoin in an inflationary bull market, gold in a stagflation bear market.
claims.direction: bitcoin in bull, gold in bear

claims.speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller
claims.quote: if it's in a bull phase, you want to own Bitcoin. But if it's in a bear phase for other assets, you want to own gold.
claims.claim: Choose Bitcoin or gold depending on whether other assets are in a bull or bear phase; he says it is 85% observation.

claims.speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller
claims.quote: Bull market geniuses.
claims.claim: Many new retail investors are bull-market geniuses riding central-bank liquidity and may be discouraged when it ends.

claims.speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller
claims.quote: it's completely contrary to what they teach in business school which is if you're highly diversified you have less risk than if you're highly concentrated.
claims.claim: He runs concentrated positions (15-20% of assets, 200-300% in macro) and monitors them daily, because stale longs/shorts are the main source of trouble.

claims.speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller
claims.quote: sizing is probably 70 to 80% of the equation.
claims.claim: From Soros: sizing is 70-80% of returns, i.e. how much you make when right and lose when wrong, not whether you are right.

claims.speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller
claims.quote: One of my number one jobs is to know whether I'm hot or cold. And when I'm hot, I'm supposed to turn the dial way up.
claims.claim: Streaks exist: size up when hot and tone down when cold rather than trying to make back losses.
claims.testable: partly - testable on a track record

claims.speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller
claims.quote: Some of them have got so cold, you can actually fade them and go the other way cuz they got themselves all twisted up.
claims.claim: Technicians also run hot and cold; follow the hot ones and fade the very cold ones.

claims.speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller
claims.quote: When you hear a good idea if you wait two or three weeks a lot of times now believe it or not 60 or 70% of the move will taken place
claims.claim: Because information spreads fast, 60-70% of a move may happen within 2-3 weeks, so he buys an idea on intuition and does research afterwards.
claims.indicator: time from idea to price move

claims.speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller
claims.quote: It would matter a lot if before they ever came in, I was already bullish on copper going three to five years out.
claims.claim: A stock idea is sized up when it fits a standing macro view (e.g. copper bullish for 3-5 years).

claims.speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller
claims.quote: I got the brilliant idea to short like 10 internet stocks which were up like seven or eightfold at Soros and I think I put 200 million into the Quantum Fund short.
claims.claim: Shorting internet stocks in March 1999 lost three to four times the investment in four weeks: shorting a bubble early is costly.

claims.speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller
claims.quote: I realized Greenspan was doing this huge easing program because of the Asian financial crisis, but there was no crisis in the United States
claims.claim: Easing with no domestic crisis, in 1999, supported the tech rally, so he went long with young specialists.

claims.speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller
claims.quote: oil is up, interest rates are up, and the dollar is up. By the way, that might sound a little familiar, and this has always been terrible for corporate earnings looking forward.
claims.claim: Rising oil, rates and dollar together have been bad for forward earnings; a regression by Ed Hyman implied -35% earnings versus consensus +18% in 2000.
claims.indicator: oil, interest rates and dollar changes

claims.speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller
claims.quote: I put 350% 10-year equivalent of the fund into um Treasuries betting that Greenspan, who has a tightening directive, will reverse
claims.claim: He took a huge long Treasury position in 2000 on the view that tightening would reverse into recession and made 40% in Q4.
claims.conditions: Fed on tightening bias but economy weakening

claims.speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller
claims.quote: If you take a break, take a break. Don't sit there and like trade your own account and mess around.
claims.claim: After large losses a total break (no screens) restored his clarity; a complete break beats grinding.

claims.speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller
claims.quote: 6-month bear markets preceded by asset bubbles don't exist historically
claims.claim: If the market rallies 15-20% he plans to short again, since 6-month bear markets after asset bubbles do not exist historically.

claims.speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller
claims.quote: Well, tell that to a labor union.
claims.claim: Excluding food and energy understates cost of living; wage settlements may embed inflation, so wage trends are a key data point.

claims.speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller
claims.quote: the next 4 to 5 years are going to be tailored to the skillset that worked for me in the in the '80s and '90s, which was all sorts of macro chaos
claims.claim: He expects macro-driven markets for the next 4-5 years.

claims.speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller
claims.quote: Do not Do not invest in the present. The present is not what moves stock prices. Change moves them.
claims.claim: Prices move on the change in expectations in 18-24 months, so envision the world in a year and a half and value off that.

claims.speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller
claims.quote: When companies are over earning, their margins are going to come down in 3 years.
claims.claim: Companies losing money cut capacity and recover margins in 3 years, while over-earners see margins mean-revert.

claims.speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller
claims.quote: this was the was the best short-selling period I've ever seen the last year or two because never before were there such obvious over-earners
claims.claim: Covid produced obvious over-earners (retail, trucking, shipping) with quadrupled stocks, giving short opportunities since retail inflows chased immediate beneficiaries.

claims.speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller
claims.quote: when they were losing money, you were supposed to buy them cuz everybody shut capacity down the next 2 or 3 years
claims.claim: In chemicals, buy when firms lose money since capacity shuts, sell when capacity expansions are announced.

claims.speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller
claims.quote: I have a bias toward growth stocks.
claims.claim: His biggest equity profits came from growth stocks he expected to be much better in 3-5 years.

claims.speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller
claims.quote: I don't care about pain trade, this or that. Um we we think these companies are still cheap relative to what we see a year or two out.
claims.claim: He stays in a crowded energy trade because the valuation versus 1-2 year earnings is cheap, and warns that 13F data is old.

claims.speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller
claims.quote: in 45 years, I've never seen a constellation while I was a practitioner or frankly studied one where there's no historical analog.
claims.claim: With no historical analog he has more humility and keeps open-mindedness to something really bad.

claims.speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller
claims.quote: I looked at a housing chart and for 50 years it went up like this and then in 5 years it went like that
claims.claim: The 2005 housing chart was a no-brainer short; the deeper they dug the more conviction, though he was wrong for six months in 2006.

claims.speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller
claims.quote: Every deflation has preceded an asset has followed an asset bubble.
claims.claim: Deflation follows an asset bubble, so the Fed's bubble creates possible 15-20 year sideways markets (1966-82) or Japan-like outcomes.

claims.speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller
claims.quote: any great short seller will tell you they made 90% of their money on the long side. The math is with you.
claims.claim: Macro investors are structurally pessimistic since they earn most in bear markets, but the math favors long positions; manage the bearish bias.

claims.speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller
claims.quote: Warren Buffett and Ken Langone, that have done quite well, say never bet against America.
claims.claim: Long-term counterpoint: never bet against America.
